column1: # malformed - dirty-climbing-trend.tsv's exact 15 rows, which ALARM at exit 1,
# preceded by a UTF-8 byte-order mark: what every Windows editor writes when it
# saves a capture. U+FEFF is not whitespace and not an id character, so the mark
# already failed closed - but as 'expected 2 fields, got 1', which invites the
# user to delete a real row. The scanner names the mark instead, and does not
# strip it: silently editing the capture it audits is the same move as silently
# dropping a row. Delete the 3 BOM bytes and this history ALARMs at 1.
